newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Newmont set to start on major Indonesia gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Newmont set to start on major Indonesia gold mine.

text.p: A top official of the U.S. Newmont Gold Company said on Wednesday that the company is set to start construction of a major new copper and gold mine in Indonesia.
"The final (government) environmental approval for the project is imminent, and we should kick off construction soon," Newmont Gold Vice-President Eric Hamer told Reuters in an interview.

The mine, on the southwest corner of Sumbawa island, will be operated by PT Newmont Nusa Tenggara, in which Newmont has a 45 percent stake, Japan's Sumitomo Corp has 35 percent and Indonesian miner PT Pukuafu Indah holds 20 percent.

A sister mine operated by PT Newmont Minahasa Raya in Northern Sulawesi poured its first gold at the end of March and expects to produce 93,000 ounces this year, Newmont Minahasa's President Director Tom Mair said.
PT Newmont Minahasa Raya is 80 percent owned by Newmont Gold and 20 percent by the Indonesian company PT Tanjung Serapung.

Hamer said production at the Sumbawa mine would start in 1999. It was expected to reach an annual output of more than 500,000 ounces of gold and 250,000 tonnes of copper concentrate during its 20-year lifespan.
The company would start taking off the over-burden in the first quarter of next year and prepare the ore body for actual mining, Hamer said.
A total of 5,500 people would be employed during the peak construction period, and the mine would employ 2,200 people when operating.

Hamer described the ore body as "low grade, high tonnage," with current reserves of 13.4 million ounces of gold and 5.3 million tonnes of copper. "This is the biggest single gold-bearing deposit Newmont has found in its history," he said.
"We think there's a lot more ore further down that will extend the mine's life," Hamer added.
Further exploration was continuing on the south-central part of Sumbawa and on the southwestern area of neighbouring Lombok island.
Hamer said the estimated capital cost of the project was $1.6 billion, rising to $1.9 billion with capitalised interest for the loans.
"We'll pay for about half, and for the rest look for financing on the markets... We're looking for financing through export-import banks," he said.
He said the milling operation would handle 120,000 tonnes of ore daily, rising to 160,000 tonnes from around 2007.
"Net operating costs will put us in the lower quartile of the world's copper production, with the gold credit against the cost of copper production," he said.
